experience.introduction: This material presents binomial expansion step by step. Each section breaks down the formulas, examples, and calculations into connected steps, preserving the source terminology and mathematical expressions.

sections.title: Title Slide
paragraphs: This is the title slide for a lesson on Expanding Binomial Expressions, presented by the Department of Computer Science. The slide displays the main topic prominently against a red background with institutional branding.

sections.title: Learning Objectives
paragraphs: The lesson has three learning objectives. By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to expand a given binomial expression with a power of a natural number, expand a given binomial expression with a power of a real number, and use binomial expansion to simplify algebraic expressions.
steps: Expand a given binomial expression with a power of a natural number.
Expand a given binomial expression with a power of a real number.
Use binomial expansion to simplify algebraic expression.

sections.title: Rationale
paragraphs: A binomial expression is usually of the form (a + b)ⁿ where a, b are algebraic terms and n is a real number. If n is a natural number, one may decide to expand the bracket by multiplying two brackets then use the result to multiply another bracket until the power of n is exhausted. This approach could be time consuming in a case of large value of n and the approach may never work when n is not a natural number. In this lesson, we present the approaches to expanding binomial expression for any value of n in the set of real numbers.
steps: Recognize that binomial expressions have the form (a + b)ⁿ with algebraic terms a, b and real number n.
Understand that repeated bracket multiplication works for natural number powers but is time consuming for large n.
Note that the repeated multiplication approach may never work when n is not a natural number.
Learn the general approaches for expanding binomial expressions for any real number n.

sections.title: Expansion Formula for Natural Number Powers
paragraphs: A binomial expression of the form (a + b)ⁿ, n ∈ ℕ can be expanded using a formula. The formula shows the expansion as a sum of terms involving binomial coefficients and powers of a and b.
steps: Identify the binomial expression (a + b)ⁿ where n is a natural number.
Apply the formula: (a + b)ⁿ equals the sum from k=0 to n of (n choose k) times aⁿ⁻ᵏ times bᵏ.
The first term is (n choose 0) aⁿ b⁰, the second is (n choose 1) aⁿ⁻¹ b¹, continuing to the last term (n choose n) a⁰ bⁿ.

sections.title: Example 1: Expanding (x + y)⁵
paragraphs: This example demonstrates the expansion of (x + y)⁵. The solution uses the binomial formula with a = x, b = y, and n = 5. The expansion produces six terms with binomial coefficients (5 choose k) for k from 0 to 5, multiplied by the appropriate powers of x and y.
steps: Identify a = x, b = y, and n = 5 in the formula.
Write out all six terms: (5 choose 0)x⁵y⁰ + (5 choose 1)x⁴y¹ + (5 choose 2)x³y² + (5 choose 3)x²y³ + (5 choose 4)xy⁴ + (5 choose 5)y⁵.
Simplify the powers: (5 choose 0)x⁵ + (5 choose 1)x⁴y + (5 choose 2)x³y² + (5 choose 3)x²y³ + (5 choose 4)xy⁴ + (5 choose 5)y⁵.

sections.title: Example 1 Continued: Computing Binomial Coefficients
paragraphs: This page defines the binomial coefficient (n choose m) as n! divided by (n−m)! times m!, and n! as n × (n−1) × (n−2) × ⋯ × 2 × 1. The page then calculates each binomial coefficient for n = 5: (5 choose 0) = 1, (5 choose 1) = 5, (5 choose 2) = 10, (5 choose 3) = 10, (5 choose 4) = 5, and (5 choose 5) = 1. Each calculation shows the factorial expansions and simplifications step by step.
steps: Define (n choose m) = n! / [(n−m)! m!] and n! = n × (n−1) × (n−2) × ⋯ × 2 × 1.
Calculate (5 choose 0) = 5! / (5! · 0!) = 1.
Calculate (5 choose 1) = 5! / (4! · 1!) = 5.
Calculate (5 choose 2) = 5! / (3! · 2!) = 10.
Calculate (5 choose 3) = 5! / (2! · 3!) = 10.
Calculate (5 choose 4) = 5! / (1! · 4!) = 5 and (5 choose 5) = 1.

sections.title: Example 1 Continued: Final Expansion and Activities
paragraphs: Substituting the binomial coefficients into the expansion gives (x + y)⁵ = 1·x⁵ + 5·x⁴y + 10·x³y² + 10·x²y³ + 5·xy⁴ + 1·y⁵. Hence, (x + y)⁵ = x⁵ + 5x⁴y + 10x³y² + 10x²y³ + 5xy⁴ + y⁵. The page includes easy activities asking how many terms the expansion has and why, what the 1st, 2nd, and 4th terms are, and what the coefficients of the 1st, 2nd, and 4th terms are.
steps: Substitute the coefficients: (x + y)⁵ = 1·x⁵ + 5·x⁴y + 10·x³y² + 10·x²y³ + 5·xy⁴ + 1·y⁵.
Simplify to obtain (x + y)⁵ = x⁵ + 5x⁴y + 10x³y² + 10x²y³ + 5xy⁴ + y⁵.
Reflect on the number of terms, identify specific terms, and determine their coefficients.

sections.title: Example 2: Expanding (2x − 3)⁴
paragraphs: This example asks for the expansion of (2x − 3)⁴ and then to evaluate (−2.998)⁴. The solution uses the binomial formula with a = 2x, b = −3, and n = 4. The expansion is written out term by term, showing the binomial coefficients (4 choose k) for k from 0 to 4, the powers of 2x, and the powers of −3. After simplification, the result is 16x⁴ − 96x³ + 216x² − 216x + 81.
steps: Identify a = 2x, b = −3, and n = 4 in the formula.
Write the expansion: (2x − 3)⁴ = (4 choose 0)(2x)⁴(−3)⁰ + (4 choose 1)(2x)³(−3)¹ + (4 choose 2)(2x)²(−3)² + (4 choose 3)(2x)(−3)³ + (4 choose 4)(−3)⁴.
Simplify powers: (4 choose 0)·16x⁴ + (4 choose 1)·8x³·(−3) + (4 choose 2)·4x²·9 + (4 choose 3)·2x·(−27) + (4 choose 4)·81.
Substitute coefficients: 1·16x⁴ + 4·8x³·(−3) + 6·4x²·9 + 4·2x·(−27) + 1·81.
Obtain the final expansion: 16x⁴ − 96x³ + 216x² − 216x + 81.

sections.title: Example 2 Continued: Evaluating (−2.998)⁴
paragraphs: To simplify (−2.998)⁴ using the expansion, compare (2x − 3)⁴ and (−2.998)⁴. This implies 2x − 3 = −2.998, so x = 0.001. Substituting x = 0.001 into the expansion 16x⁴ − 96x³ + 216x² − 216x + 81 gives (−2.998)⁴ = (2(0.001) − 3)⁴ = 16(0.001)⁴ − 96(0.001)³ + 216(0.001)² − 216(0.001) + 81 = 80.7842. Hence, (−2.998)⁴ = 80.7842.
steps: Compare (2x − 3)⁴ and (−2.998)⁴ to find 2x − 3 = −2.998.
Solve for x: x = 0.001.
Substitute x = 0.001 into 16x⁴ − 96x³ + 216x² − 216x + 81.

sections.title: Student Activity: Practice Problems
paragraphs: Two practice problems are provided. The first asks to find the coefficient of the 4th term in the expansion of (2 − (1/4)x²)⁶. The second asks to evaluate the 5th term in the expansion of (4x − 3y)⁸.
steps: Find the coefficient of the 4th term in the expansion of (2 − (1/4)x²)⁶.
Evaluate the 5th term in the expansion of (4x − 3y)⁸.

sections.title: Solution to Student Activity
paragraphs: For the first problem, the 4th term is (6 choose 3)·2³·(−(1/4)x²)³ = (6 choose 3)·8·(−1/64)x⁶. Computing (6 choose 3) = 6×5×4×3! / (3×2×1·3!) gives 20. Thus the 4th term is 20·8·(−1/64)x⁶ = −(20/8)x⁶, so the coefficient is −20/8. For the second problem, the 5th term is (8 choose 4)·(4x)⁴·(−3y)⁴. Wait, the source shows (8 choose 5)·(4x)³·(−3y)⁵. Computing (8 choose 5) = 8×7×6×5! / (3×2×1·5!) = 56. Then 56·64x³·(−243y⁵) = −870,912x³y⁵.
steps: For problem 1, the 4th term is (6 choose 3)·2³·(−(1/4)x²)³ = (6 choose 3)·8·(−1/64)x⁶.
Calculate (6 choose 3) = 20, giving −(20/8)x⁶ as the 4th term with coefficient −20/8.
For problem 2, the 5th term is (8 choose 4)·(4x)⁴·(−3y)⁴, but the source shows (8 choose 5)·(4x)³·(−3y)⁵.
Calculate (8 choose 5) = 56, then 56·64x³·(−243y⁵) = −870,912x³y⁵.

sections.title: Expansion Formula for Real Number Powers
paragraphs: In cases where the power n of a given binomial expression is negative or fraction, we transform the binomial expression into the form (1 − x)ⁿ then use the formula: (1 − x)ⁿ = 1 − nx + [n(n−1)/2!]x² − [n(n−1)(n−2)/3!]x³ + ⋯. An example is given: Find the binomial expansion of (1 + 3x)⁻⁴ to the fourth term.
steps: Recognize that for negative or fractional n, transform the expression into the form (1 − x)ⁿ.
Apply the formula: (1 − x)ⁿ = 1 − nx + [n(n−1)/2!]x² − [n(n−1)(n−2)/3!]x³ + ⋯.
Use this formula to expand (1 + 3x)⁻⁴ to the fourth term.

sections.title: Solution to Example 1: Expanding (1 + 3x)⁻⁴
paragraphs: Given (1 + 3x)⁻⁴, comparing with (1 − x)ⁿ we have 3x = −x and −4 = n. Using the formula (1 − x)ⁿ = 1 − nx + [n(n−1)/2!]x² − [n(n−1)(n−2)/3!]x³ + ⋯, substitute to get (1 − (−3x))⁻⁴ = 1 − (−4)(−3x) + [(−4)(−4−1)/2!](−3x)² − [(−4)(−4−1)(−4−2)/3!](−3x)³ + ⋯. Simplifying gives 1 − 12x + (20/2)·9x² − (120/6)·27x³ + ⋯ = 1 − 12x + 90x² − 540x³ + ⋯.
steps: Compare (1 + 3x)⁻⁴ with (1 − x)ⁿ to find 3x = −x and n = −4.
Obtain the expansion: 1 − 12x + 90x² − 540x³ + ⋯.

sections.title: Student Activity: Expanding (1 − 2x)^(1/2)
paragraphs: The activity asks to find the binomial expansion of (1 − 2x)^(1/2) to the fourth term.
steps: Find the binomial expansion of (1 − 2x)^(1/2) to the fourth term.

sections.title: Solution to Student Activity: Expanding (1 − 2x)^(1/2)
steps: Compare (1 − 2x)^(1/2) with (1 − x)ⁿ to find 2x = x and n = 1/2.
Simplify to obtain (1 − 2x)^(1/2) = 1 − x − (1/2)x² − (1/2)x³ + ⋯.

sections.title: Summary
paragraphs: In this lecture, the following concepts are covered: binomial expressions, binomial expansion, binomial coefficients and terms, algebraic application of binomial expansion, and binomial expansion with negative or fractional power.
steps: Binomial expressions
Binomial expansion
Binomial coefficients and terms
Algebraic application of binomial expansion
Binomial expansion with negative or fractional power
